page: Amazon Web Services r8i.96xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 384 vCPUs and 192 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The system includes 3072.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8i.96xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, achieving high scores in stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong, with uncached read speeds reaching 1125.32 GB/sec and cached read speeds at 30551.22 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, alongside static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance and PassMark memory scores fall into the average range.

The instance presents specific architectural tradeoffs. While it excels at prompt processing for large language models, text generation speeds for smaller models are poor, registering at 34.24 tokens/sec. The absence of local storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached alternatives, which may impact latency-sensitive I/O workloads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of DDR5 memory and massive vCPU count make it a resource-dense option for large-scale, memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe drives.

This server is suited for memory-intensive applications, including large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, and complex software compilation. It is also highly capable for multi-threaded data decompression, ray tracing, and LLM prompt processing tasks.
